_why: `go test ./...` exits 0 when it ran nothing. Measured at 5eb2829: with all 23
*_test.go files moved aside, the direct required lane exited 0 with 22 packages
reporting `[no test files]` (PR#6 VERIFY, FINDING 3). These floors are what make
that red. They are a FLOOR, not an expected count: they exist to catch a suite
being emptied or a package disappearing, not to pin churn.
PER-PACKAGE FLOORS COVER EVERY PACKAGE. A whole-suite floor alone does NOT detect
one package disappearing: the PR#9 verifier measured 1047 unit tests against a
floor of 900 at e710c3c, and twelve of fourteen packages fitted inside that
headroom — internal/obs (the redaction suite) and internal/httpapi included
(PR#9 VERIFY, FINDING 7). The integration suite is a SUPERSET of the unit suite —
the build tag only ADDS files — so its whole-suite number says little about the
integration tests themselves. A package that RUNS with no floor recorded here is
refused, so a new package cannot arrive unprotected.
MEASURED in CI (ubuntu-24.04, GNU Make 4.3, go1.27.1, `go test -race -count=1 -json`) on
d435cd8, the round-3 head, and printed by scripts/go-test-report.py itself:
unit         (./...)                     1109 executed, 195 top-level, 0 skips

Round 2's per-package floors were GENERATED with `--emit-floors` (15% headroom, at
least 2 tests of slack, never below 1) from 1071/1116. In round 3 only the packages
whose counts moved were regenerated: `scripts` 128 -> 161, and the whole-suite floors
910/949 -> 943/981. One deliberate exception: the generator proposed 38 for
internal/integration, but 40 was already committed at e710c3c, and a floor is never
lowered to fit a generator — so it stays 40. Floors only rise.
Lowering a floor, or adding an allowed_skips entry, is a REVIEWED diff. An empty
allowed_skips is the correct state: a required test that is skipped is not a pass
(AGENTS.md). Both suites have zero skips today, and `make test-integration` FAILS
rather than skipping when its services are absent, so there is nothing to allow.
To regenerate after the suites grow (then never set a floor below its current value):
go test -count=1 -json ./... > e.json; echo $? > x.txt
python3 scripts/go-test-report.py --events e.json --suite unit \
--floors scripts/test-floors.json --go-exit-file x.txt --emit-floors
